entries.english: 21 Kossova (Kisii / Abagusii) Clans & 1900 Chiefs Recorded by C. W. Hobley (1902, pp. 50–51)
entries.translation: (1) Ugirango (chief Yawanga), (2) Mukimusi (Kimaina), (3) Msasuri (Munari), (4) Magichana (Borura), (5) Manweni (Minyigo), (6) Mkanyimbo (Uturi & Mtaruki), (7) Nyaliwali (Yamombo), (8) Mowasi (Maina), (9) Umachogi (Kitubo), (10) Mukura (Maina & Ndieki), (11) Ukeiri (Mwesaba), (12) Wa Koma (Mwakwega), (13) Woyeki (Sianyo), (14) Mwachawi (Samevita), (15) Ukitaa (Morema), (16) Umwaliwa (Uroo), (17) Umulenda (Munyanja), (18) Mugika (Wato), (19) Yamugei (Sakawa), (20) Mugusero (Umbachi), (21) Matala (Siambe), plus Chief Kitoto of the Kitoto (Kano) plain noted as a pure-bred Kisii (p. 9)
entries.pronunciation: u-gi-ran-go / u-ma-cho-gi / u-ki-ta-a / ya-mu-ge-i / sa-ka-wa / mu-gu-se-ro
entries.context: C. W. Hobley (1902) 'Eastern Uganda: An Ethnological Survey', Ch. I p. 9 & Ch. V § 1 pp. 50–51

entries.english: 6 Noun Classes in Kossova (Kisii) Recorded by C. W. Hobley (1902, p. 86)
entries.translation: Class I um- → aw- (umuntu → awantu 'person → people', umkungu → awakungu 'woman → women'); Class II o- → mi- (okuwoko → mikowoko 'arm → arms') & u- → i- (umogwe → imegwe 'arrow → arrows', umuchi → imichi 'town → towns'); Class III unchanged (muriro 'fire'); Class IV iki-, ichi- → ivi- (ikisiri → ivisiri 'axe → axes', ichiara → iviara 'finger → fingers', ikirandi → ivirandi 'gourd → gourds'); Class V u- → ama- (uwusio → amasio 'face → faces'), li-, ili- → ma-, ama- (liliga → amaliga 'tear → tears', ligina → amagina 'stone/egg → stones/eggs', ilikori → amakori 'path → paths'), ki- → mi- (kisimba → misimba 'cat → cats'), e-, l- → ama- (erino/lino → amaino 'ivory/tooth → teeth'); Class VI e-, i- → chi-, achi-, si- (imbandi → chimbandi 'groundnut', enjoka → chinjoka 'snake', enzwi → sinzwi 'fish', engoko → achingoko 'fowl', imburi → achimburi 'goat')
entries.pronunciation: u-mun-tu a-wan-tu / i-ki-si-ri i-vi-si-ri / li-gi-na a-ma-gi-na / im-bu-ri a-chim-bu-ri
entries.context: C. W. Hobley (1902) 'Eastern Uganda: An Ethnological Survey', Ch. VI, p. 86

entries.english: Kossova (Kisii) Vocabulary, Numerals, Pronouns & Verb Phrases (Hobley 1902, pp. 89–91)
entries.translation: Lexicon (pp. 89–91): iviricha (God), iriuba (sky), insoih (sun), umweri (moon), tzinini (stars), imvula (rain), amachi (water), isekawa (chief), amaemba (dhurra/mtama), owoli (wimbi), matoki (banana), amarua (beer), kisale (twins) • Numerals (p. 91): 1 ejemo, 2 wa-wili / chi-wili, 3 wa-tatu / chi-tatu, 4 wa-nne / chi-nne, 5 tano, 6 tano na emo, 7 tano na eviri, 8 tano na etatu, 9 kienda, 10 ekumi, 20 makumiyawiri, 100 emirongo ekumi • Pronouns & Verbs (p. 91): ninchi (I), nururi (thou), nururio (he), nitwi (we), ninwi (you), embabu (they); ncha hano (come here), genda (go away), ninchi nagenda (I go), narorire (I have seen)
entries.pronunciation: i-vi-ri-cha / i-se-ka-wa / e-je-mo / wa-wi-li / ki-en-da / e-ku-mi / n-cha ha-no
entries.context: C. W. Hobley (1902) 'Eastern Uganda: An Ethnological Survey', Ch. VII § I, pp. 89–91

entries.english: Sir Harry Johnston's (1919–1922) Sub-Group A 6 (#7 Ki-guzii & #7a Ki-kωria) & #8 Ki-šaši Comparative Corpus
entries.translation: Vowel Lowering & Prefixes (Vol. I, p. 85 & Vol. II, pp. 24–25): Replacement of i by e and u by ω in prefixes (Ωmω-/Ava-, Ωmω-/Eme-, Eri-/Ama-, Eke-[Ege-]/Evi-, E-[En-]/Ci-[Cin-], Ωrω-/Cin-, Eke- [Class 13 dim.], Ωbω-, Ωkω-/Ωgω-) • Numerals (p. 81): #7 Ki-guzii uses quinary 6–8 (-sanω na i-mω, -sanω na i-were, -sanω na i-satu, ki-anda, i-kumi/ωmu-roṅgω), whereas #7a Ki-kωria uses -sansaba (6), mu-huṅgati (7), mω-nane (8), ki-anda/k-enda (9), i-kumi/ωmu-roṅgu (10), eri-gana (100) • Distinctive A 6 Roots (pp. 73–80): Eri-gωmia/Eri-tωki (banana), Amany-iṅga/Ama-sere (#7a) (blood), Eri/Ici-eri (bull), Omw-ami/Ωmu-nda/Umw-isia (#7) vs. Ωmω-kama (#7a) (chief), E-sese (dog), Eke-reṅge/Eke-sanyi (foot/hand), Omw-iseke/Ωmω-subati (girl/sister), Eri-uba/Ivi-rica/Eny-asai (God), Iny-anaω (#7) vs. E-ṅiti (#7a) (hyena), Eke-iri/Eṅ-gō (#7) vs. Eri-gwe (#7a) (leopard), Ωmu-tienyi (#7) vs. Ωmu-eri (#7a) (moon), Ωmu-basu (sun), Eki-sare (twins)
entries.context: Sir Harry H. Johnston, 'A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages' (Vol. I, 1919, pp. 73–97; Vol. II, 1922, pp. 24–26, 497–498)
